Subject: Pen test triggers & audit scope questions for MSA/Order Form

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form last week. Our legal and security teams reviewed the security exhibit and had a few open questions before we can proceed to procurement:

1) Pen test triggers — the current draft ties a "right to inspect" and full pen test to a vague "material change" clause. Can you clarify what would actually trigger a full-scope pen test and what the notice windows would look like? We want to avoid open-ended inspection rights without clear boundaries.

2) SOC 2 evidence cadence — the exhibit references "regular reports" but doesn't specify frequency or delivery mechanism. Would Redwood be open to a quarterly evidence cadence for operational controls (summary) and annual full SOC 2 reports?

3) Staging & ephemeral access — are there predefined carve-outs for staging systems or ephemeral environments? If a pen test is required, what access / scope is expected for non-production?

We're attaching a short list of our procurement constraints and a redline from our counsel (attached). Happy to jump on a short call.

Attachments: Medallion_procs_constraints.pdf (pdf), Medallion_proposed_redline.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Christine Park
Head of Security Programs
Medallion Health

Subject: Re: Pen test triggers & audit scope questions for MSA/Order Form

Christine — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Looping in Karthik and Laura from legal to weigh in on firm language. Quick responses below and a proposed path forward.

High level proposal (summary):
- Pen test trigger: replace vague "material change" with an "Embedded Trigger" approach — a named list of events that can trigger a full-scope test (major infra migration, change of cloud tenancy, external-facing control-plane changes) plus a residual "reasonable suspicion" clause that requires documented incidents to justify an extra test.
- Notice & scheduling: 30 days notice for scheduling; Redwood commits to a scheduling window of 60 days from notice (we can offer a 30-day expedited option for mutually agreed critical cases). No more than one full-scope customer-initiated external penetration test per 12-month period unless mutually agreed or there is evidence of compromise.
- SOC 2 / evidence cadence: we can provide the full SOC 2 Type II annually and an operational evidence summary (controls snapshot) quarterly. Access to underlying evidence can be provided via a secure evidence portal for a 90-day window following request.
- Staging carve-outs: agree to limit full-scope external testing to production and production-adjacent environments unless customer explicitly requests staging to be included; staging requests will be scoped as separate work with an access plan.

I'll attach our draft redlines to the MSA exhibit (MSA_redlines_v3.pdf) and a suggested cadence workbook (proposed-evidence-cadence.xlsx). Please review and tell us which of the embedded triggers you accept or want edited.

Next steps: if acceptable, Karthik / Laura can incorporate the final language into the MSA redline and we can present a short playbook (1-page) to procurement.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Sr. Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_redlines_v3.pdf, proposed-evidence-cadence.xlsx

Thanks — quick legal perspective and an excerpt of proposed contract text below for Rachael/Christine to review.

Recommended contract approach (legal):
- Define "Embedded Triggers" enumerated (example list): (a) migration of customer data between cloud providers; (b) changes to public API authentication model; (c) onboarding of third-party subsystems with privileged access to customer data; (d) verified security incident affecting confidentiality/integrity availability for that customer's tenant.
- Add timing guardrails: "Customer shall provide written notice; Redwood shall respond with proposed schedule within 10 business days; target completion within 60 calendar days from mutual scheduling. Customer-initiated testing limited to one full-scope test per rolling 12 months unless evidence of compromise or mutual written agreement."
- Evidence access: "Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report within 10 business days of request for customers with executed NDA/order form; detailed control evidence will be available via secure portal for a 90-day review window. Any request for forensic access or privileged credentials shall be processed under a separate access agreement and will require advance scheduling and agreed scope."

Proposed redline excerpt (to add to security exhibit):
"If Customer requests a customer-initiated penetration test beyond routine scanning, the request must identify the Embedded Trigger category. Redwood will engage its security operations team and, where appropriate, provide a mutually-agreed statement of work that limits scope to relevant systems. Redwood reserves the right to require a scoped, remote-only assessment when access to production systems would cause unacceptable risk. Full-scope tests requiring privileged credentials or access to systems containing non-customer data will be scheduled with an access plan and additional controls."

Couple of notes for procurement: keep the "one per 12 months" default — it's an easy carveout for most customers and reduces operational churn for redwood. Also push the evidence portal idea to reduce file-transfer overhead.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Adding ops/legal operational constraints and a suggested acceptance criteria for limited vs full inspections.

Operational suggestions:
- SOC 2 cadence: SOC 2 Type II delivered annually by secure portal link + quarterly customer-facing control summary (one page) delivered via email.
- Evidence portal access: request window opens with 10 business days' notice; Redwood provides evidence bundle within 7 business days of access being granted; evidence is accessible for 90 days.
- Limited inspections (samples) vs full inspections: define a threshold (e.g., incident severity score or business impact) that elevates a request to full inspection; otherwise, accept a control sampling review and vendor-attested remediation plan.
- Staging: explicitly exclude customer-initiated full-scope tests on completed staging unless customer pays for a scoped engagement and provides test credentials.

I'll prepare a concise one-page playbook for procurement that captures "what triggers what" and the scheduling/ops flow (request -> triage -> schedule -> evidence window -> post-test checklist). That playbook will live at the Drive link I added in the related_links metadata.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
